title: O mnie, o tobie, ze mną
title_en: Me and you, after a preposition
note:
C1 Block 3, unit 2 (C1-SPINE). THE FIRST AND SECOND PERSON AFTER A PREPOSITION - the half of the row b2_pron_prep [141] deliberately did not build, and it named this unit as its own alternative in its own note: 'THE UNIT'S ONE REAL JUDGMENT CALL, and the conservative branch was taken: THIRD PERSON ONLY. o mnie, o tobie, ze mna, z toba, do ciebie, z nami, z wami appear nowhere... THE ALTERNATIVE, if James wants it: a small b2_pron_prep2 with those six forms and the ze-rule.' This is that unit, one level on, and it also pays the older fence a2_o_loc wrote ('the unit says about work / about home, never about you. They need their own small unit') - the half b2_pron_prep left standing.

SIX NEW STRINGS, exactly as many as b2_pron_prep had: mna, tobie, ciebie, toba, nami, wami. Plus ZE, which is a fact about the preposition rather than the pronoun and is the reason b2_pron_prep called this 'the do/z cliff in miniature'.

THE UNIT'S ONE IDEA IS AN ASYMMETRY, and it is what keeps six new forms down to one new thing: TWO OF THE THREE CASES COST ALMOST NOTHING. After o and after do, ja, my and wy reuse the very strings the learner already has as objects - mnie, nas, was (b2_pron_acc [140]) - so the entire Locative and Genitive of three persons out of four is already in his mouth. ONLY ty is genuinely different, and it is different twice (tobie after o, ciebie after do). The Instrumental is where the new words actually are: mna, toba, nami, wami, four for four. Slide 2 is that table and slide 3 is the Instrumental.

THE ANCHOR IS REAL AND WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: wedlug mnie is TAUGHT <- b2_discussion_func as a whole phrase, so the learner has been putting a first-person pronoun after a preposition for a level already - it simply happened to be the only cell he had. Same 'you already say this' opener b2_adj_acc, b2_verbal_nouns and c1_na_acc use.

NEW JOBS ON OWNED STRINGS, named rather than smuggled: mnie is TAUGHT <- a2_dat_chunks [83] inside boli mnie (the accusative-experiencer chunk) and generalised by b2_pron_acc [140] as the ordinary Accusative object; here it is the LOCATIVE after o and the GENITIVE after do. nas and was are TAUGHT <- b2_pron_acc as Accusatives and do the same two jobs here. That the string does not change is the unit's gift and slide 2 says so outright, rather than leaving the learner to wonder whether he has missed a form.

THE ze RULE IS STATED AS A CLOSED FACT, NOT A PRODUCTIVE RULE, on the gen_pl_full fleeting-e precedent C1-SPINE cites for exactly this genre. What is claimed: Polish says ze mna and never z mna, and the learner already does this in ze szkoly, ze sklepu, ze szpitala (a1_prep_do_z, TAUGHT as frozen chunks). What is also claimed, because it is true and it is what makes the fact safe: mna is THE ONLY PRONOUN this happens to - z toba, z nami, z wami all keep the plain z, and so does every third-person form he learned last level. No attempt is made to state the phonological condition; a learner who cannot trust a rule gets no value from it.

THE SHORT FORMS ARE FENCED POSITIONALLY, NOT BY EMPHASIS, and this was the unit's sharpest scope decision. cie and ci (b2_pron_acc, b1_dative_pron) sit next to the verb; ciebie and tobie follow a preposition. That is ALL slide 4 claims. The stressed/emphatic use of the long forms - Ciebie znam - is C1-SPINE's explicit property of c1_word_order ('sentence-initial emphatic jego/ciebie'), three nodes on, and appears nowhere here. Quiz item 10 runs the discrimination in the OTHER direction (Znam ___ -> cie, not ciebie) so the positional rule is drilled both ways rather than only as 'the long one is the new one'.

THE DATIVE IS NOT OPENED, holding b2_pron_prep's own reason verbatim: no preposition in this course governs the Dative, so a prepositional Dative pronoun has nowhere to sit. tobie appears ONLY as the Locative after o. The long-vs-short Dative contrast (mi/mnie, ci/tobie) is not raised anywhere.

ONE EXTRA GOVERNOR, taken deliberately and logged as this unit's judgment call: od in its COMPARISON job (a2_superlatives [91], starszy od brata). It costs zero new pronoun forms - od takes the Genitive, so it takes do's forms - and it buys Brat jest starszy od ciebie, a sentence this learner will actually say. Exposure is held to ONE slide row, ONE match item and ONE use item; od appears in no Pisanie item and no Kontrola distractor. The SOURCE job of od (list od siostry) is c1_od_source's property and is not hinted at.

HELD FENCES from b2_pron_prep, all still verified NEW: dla (a governor the course has never taught - that pack dropped it from B2-SPINE's own illustrative example, and the same catch applies here); w and na + pronoun; niemu. siebie/sobie are c1_siebie's, one node on, and appear nowhere - which matters here more than anywhere, because ze mna and z soba are one letter apart in the learner's future.

AUDITOR NOTE, and it CORRECTS C1-SPINE: the spine's standing fence says 'Person pronouns sit in audit.py's GLUE_LEMMAS, so the auditor cannot see a single pronoun fence in Block 3.' That is only half true and was checked rather than trusted - GLUE_LEMMAS holds the bare SUBJECT pronouns (ja, ty, on, ona, ono, my, wy, oni, one) and nothing else, so every oblique form in this unit (mnie, cie, ci, nas, was, tobie, ciebie, mna, toba, nami, wami) IS visible to the auditor and IS policed. The fence that genuinely remains author-only is the subject pronouns, which appear nowhere in this pack.

PISANIE: eight cloze items, one per new string plus the ze item, so ALL EIGHT blank the teaching point and there is no fallback anywhere - the first unit in the level where the count of distinct new forms matches the stage exactly. No typed-whole answers; nothing added to the repair queue.

TITLE CHECKED AT THE WIRE: O mnie, o tobie, ze mna - o TAUGHT <- a2_o_loc, mnie TAUGHT <- a2_dat_chunks, and tobie / ze / mna are all taught by this pack itself (the c1_adj_pl_gen precedent). No untaught Polish in learner-visible chrome.

SECOND TOOLING ARTIFACT, same genre as the one C1-SPINE documents for na: the bare preposition DO is not a lemma anywhere in the course - it lives only inside multi-word lemmas (do sklepu, do domu, do pracy, do matki) and its Genitive job is carried by the prep_do_gen STRUCTURE. Declaring it in uses_lemmas produced a real audit error on the first run and the fix is to drop it, not to 'teach' it: do has been on screen since A1. o and od are NOT affected - both exist as bare lemmas in the pool and are declared normally.

intro.title: The row about you and me
intro.title_pl: o mnie · ze mną · do ciebie
intro.body:
Last level you learned what him, her and them look like after a preposition: o nim, z nią, do nich. The same sentence about yourself, or about the person you are speaking to, had no forms at all.

You do already say one of them. Since B2 you have had według mnie — "in my opinion" — which is a first-person pronoun sitting after a preposition. It was simply the only cell you owned.

Here is the rest of it. Three prepositions, each keeping the case it has always had: o takes the Locative, z takes the Instrumental, do takes the Genitive.

intro.title: Two of the three cases cost you almost nothing
intro.body:
Look at what actually changes. After o and after do, three of the four persons use the very word you already use as an object: mnie, nas, was. You have said Boli mnie głowa since A2 and Znam was since B2, and those are the same strings.

So the Locative and the Genitive of ja, my and wy are already yours. Nothing to learn.

Only ty is different, and it is different in two ways: after o it is tobie, after do it is ciebie. That one person is where the work is.

examples.en: The doctor is talking about us.

intro.title: The Instrumental is where the new words are
intro.title_pl: ze mną · z tobą · z nami · z wami
intro.body:
After z all four are new: mną, tobą, nami, wami.

And one of them changes the preposition. Polish says ze mną, never z mną. You have been doing this since A1 without being told: ze szkoły, ze sklepu, ze szpitala — z grows an -e when the word after it would be hard to say against it.

The useful part is how narrow it is. mną is the only pronoun this happens to. z tobą, z nami, z wami all keep the plain z, and so does every him/her/them form you learned last level.

rows: ze — the only pronoun that does this

intro.title: The short ones never follow a preposition
intro.body:
cię and ci are short because they live right beside the verb: Znam cię.

A preposition will not take them. After o, do or z, Polish reaches for the longer word instead — o tobie, do ciebie, z tobą. There is no o cię and no do cię.

This is about position and nothing else. Which of the two you use is decided by whether a preposition is standing in front of the slot.

examples.en: A friend is going to your place.

intro.title: In a real sentence — and one more preposition
intro.body:
od has been making comparisons since A2: starszy od brata. It takes the Genitive, so it takes exactly the forms do takes — od ciebie, od mnie, od nas.

That gives you a sentence worth having: Brat jest starszy od ciebie.

Everything below is built out of prepositions and verbs you already own. The only part that is new is the pronoun on the end.
intro.body_pl: od + dopełniacz = te same formy co do

rows: Anna is driving to your place.
My brother is older than you.

examples.en: The children are going with you.

match.en: The doctor is talking about us.
The students are talking about you.
A friend is going to your place.
Mum is coming to my place.

quiz.prompt: Mama mówi o ___. (Mum is talking about me.)
quiz.explain: o takes the Locative, and for ja that is mnie — the same string you already use as an object in Boli mnie głowa. mną would need z in front of it.

quiz.prompt: Tata myśli o ___. (Dad is thinking about you.)
quiz.explain: ty is the one person that does not reuse its object form here. After o it is tobie; ciebie belongs after do, and cię never follows a preposition at all.

quiz.prompt: Brat pracuje ___ mną. (My brother works with me.)
quiz.explain: Polish says ze mną, never z mną — the same -e you already say in ze szkoły and ze sklepu. mną is the only pronoun this happens to.

quiz.prompt: Koleżanka pracuje z ___. (My colleague works with you.)
quiz.explain: z has taken the Instrumental since A2 and nothing changes for a pronoun. tobie is the Locative, which would need o.

quiz.prompt: Siostra mieszka z ___. (My sister lives with us.)
quiz.explain: The Instrumental is the one case where every person gets a new word. nas is the object form and works after o and do, but not after z.

quiz.prompt: Dzieci mieszkają z ___. (The children live with you.)
quiz.explain: Same shape as nami, one person along. was is the form for o and do.

quiz.prompt: Kolega idzie do ___. (A friend is going to your place.)
quiz.explain: do takes the Genitive, and for ty that is ciebie. This is the second of the two forms ty has — tobie is the other one, and it goes after o.

quiz.prompt: Lekarz mówi o ___. (The doctor is talking about us.)
quiz.explain: Nothing new here at all: after o, my keeps the object form nas. Only ty changes.

quiz.prompt: Studenci mówią o ___. (The students are talking about you.)
quiz.explain: Same as the item before, for wy. wami is the Instrumental and would need z.
The other direction, and it is the one to watch: there is no preposition here, so the short form is right. ciebie would only be correct with do, od or another preposition in front of it.

quiz.prompt: Brat jest starszy od ___. (My brother is older than you.)
quiz.explain: od takes the Genitive, exactly as do does, so it takes the same form: ciebie. This is the comparison od you have used since starszy od brata.

quiz.prompt: Mama idzie do ___. (Mum is coming to our place.)
quiz.explain: do takes the Genitive and my reuses its object form there, so nas covers both o and do.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The doctor is talking about you.

use_items.explain: Plain z here — the -e appears only before mną. The Instrumental of my is nami.

use_items.explain: wami, not was: z has taken the Instrumental since A2 and a pronoun is no exception.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Anna is driving to your place.
use_items.explain: do has taken the Genitive since A1 — do sklepu, do domu, and now do ciebie.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Mum is coming to our place.
use_items.explain: The Genitive of my is nas — the object form again. Three of the four persons cost nothing after do.

use_items.explain: od takes the Genitive just as do does, so the form is the same one: ciebie. This is the comparison od from starszy od brata.
tobą after z, tobie after o, ciebie after do — three prepositions, three different shapes, and ty is the only person that makes you keep track.
